effect_on_paper_claims: Blocks any claim that the attention path trains, and weakens the existing one-batch attention training contract, which observes the packed array only.
expectation: A parameter that the optimizer updates must change in the layer that consumes it.
measured_impact: The packed graph array changes while all four attention projections are unchanged, so attention contributes nothing to the learned function.

measurements.consequence: After any number of optimizer steps the attention projections used by the forward pass are unchanged, so the attention block does not train.

minimal_reproduction: Build Embedding->Attention(1 head)->RNN->sigmoid Dense with a fixed seed, run one TrainingEngine.train_batch with SGD at lr=0.05, and compare the layer's W_q/W_k/W_v/W_o before and after.
recommended_remediation: Correct AttentionLayer.set_params to accept the rank-3 packed layout its own params() exposes (or have params() return the rank-4 layout set_params expects), and add a regression test asserting the projections move.
title: Attention projection updates never reach the attention layer

effect_on_paper_claims: The system must not be described as supporting multi-head attention.
expectation: A requested architecture parameter must change the computation.
measured_impact: Outputs are identical and the attention weight matrix has a single head's shape.

measurements.consequence: A user selecting two or more heads receives single-head computation with no warning. Multi-head attention is not implemented.

minimal_reproduction: Build two graphs differing only in num_heads (1 versus 2), copy identical projections into both, and compare outputs.
recommended_remediation: Either implement head splitting and per-head concatenation, or reject num_heads > 1 in validate_layers with an explicit error.
title: num_heads is accepted but has no effect

effect_on_paper_claims: Any vector-input BatchNorm graph must be reported as degenerate; the parameter-count and FLOP estimates in validate_layers remain valid but the layer is functionally an identity-plus-bias in that regime.
expectation: A normalisation layer should transform its input and propagate gradient.
measured_impact: The output equals beta for every input and the input gradient is exactly zero, so no parameter below the layer can train through it.

measurements.consequence: With a vector input the normalisation is degenerate: the layer output equals beta for every input, the input gradient is exactly zero, and no parameter below the layer can receive gradient through it.

minimal_reproduction: Build Input(5)->BatchNorm->Output(2), feed two different 5-vectors, and compare the BatchNorm output and the backward input gradient.
recommended_remediation: Reject vector-input BatchNorm at validation time, or implement a running-statistics inference mode so the layer is usable outside a spatial context.
title: Batch normalisation degenerates on vector inputs

effect_on_paper_claims: The paper must not claim that the simulator's forward/trace workflow covers convolutional or recurrent architectures through the application route.
expectation: A route must be able to express the inputs of the architectures it accepts.
measured_impact: The route raises an unpacking error while the engine accepts the same graph with a nested payload, so the visible forward-execution path is limited to flat vector inputs.

measurements.consequence: The forward trace route cannot express the nested inputs that spatial and sequence graphs require, so those graphs are not executable through the route even though the engine accepts them directly.

route_payload_flat_list.exception: ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 1)

minimal_reproduction: POST /api/simulator/forward/full with a List[float] payload for a graph whose input_shape is [1,5,5]; then call run_forward_full directly with a nested payload.
recommended_remediation: Change the request model to accept a nested array (or accept an explicit input_shape alongside a flat vector), and add a route test per input rank.
title: Forward trace route cannot express spatial or sequence inputs

effect_on_paper_claims: The identifier must not be described as an architecture fingerprint or used as an experiment identity.
expectation: An architecture identifier must distinguish architectures.
measured_impact: Distinct architectures produce the same 12-character hash.

measurements.consequence: architecture_hash cannot identify an architecture: it collides across distinct layer types, activations and output widths that share a neuron count signature.

minimal_reproduction: Build four architectures that share a neuron-count signature but differ in activation, output width or layer type, and compare architecture_hash.
recommended_remediation: Hash a canonical serialisation of the full layer configuration, including layer types, activations and non-neuron fields.
title: architecture_hash collides across distinct architectures

effect_on_paper_claims: Reported as a declared boundary rather than a defect; no batching claim is made.
expectation: A leading batch dimension is either supported or explicitly unsupported.
measured_impact: The dense layer reshapes its input to one dimension and the matmul fails.

measurements.consequence: The dense layer flattens its input, so the batch dimension is not supported anywhere on the dense path. Reported as a declared boundary.
measurements.exception: ValueError: matmul: Input operand 1 has a mismatch in its core dimension 0, with gufunc signature (n?,k),(k,m?)->(n?,m?) (size 9 is different from 3)

minimal_reproduction: Call graph.forward with a (3, 3) array on Input(3)->Dense(4)->Output(2).
recommended_remediation: Document the boundary in the API contract, or reshape explicitly to (batch, features) and propagate batched gradients.
title: Dense path has no batch dimension

effect_on_paper_claims: Convolution configurations using 'same' with stride > 1 are not comparable with framework implementations and must not be presented as such.
expectation: A declared padding mode should match the conventional meaning of that mode.
measured_impact: The simulator produces a 5x5 output where the conventional rule gives 3x3; with the simulator's own geometry the arithmetic matches the reference.

measurements.consequence: With stride greater than one the simulator's 'same' padding does not produce the conventional ceil(in/stride) output size, so the declared padding mode does not mean what a framework user expects.

minimal_reproduction: Compare a stride-2 'same' convolution against an independent float64 reference using both the conventional and the simulator's geometry.
recommended_remediation: Adopt the framework convention (ceil(in/stride)) or rename the mode so the non-standard geometry is explicit.
title: 'same' padding with stride greater than one is non-standard
